statement: Finite ordered binary trees carry real leaf values and real internal labels. Define E(leaf(x))=x and E(add(a,b,d))=(E(a)+E(b))(1+d); define F(leaf(x))=[x] and F(add(a,b,d))=F(a) concatenated with F(b). The construction repeatedly pairs the first half of the current tree list with the second half at equal offsets, keeping an unmatched tree. Starting from input leaves, it runs a ceiling-logarithmic number of rounds and selects the first tree. The targets assert a bounded additive perturbation representation for the returned tree and a length identity for arbitrary round counts. The perturbation representation is indexed by the resulting tree leaf order, with no stated equality of that order to the input order.

targets.name: Bhola.algorithm_leaf_backward_error
targets.statement: For every finite list xs of real numbers and every function err: N x N -> R, if xs is nonempty, then for every real u, if u >= 0, |err(l,j)| <= u for all l,j in N, and h*u < 1 where h=clog_2(length(xs)), there exists a tree t with algorithm(xs,err)=some(t), and there exists a finite list ps of pairs of real numbers such that map(first,ps)=F(t), E(t)=sum_{(a,e) in ps}(a+e), and for every pair (a,e) belonging to ps, |e| <= gamma(h,u)*|a|. The sum counts list occurrences; the first-coordinate list has the order and multiplicity of F(t). Here gamma(h,u)=(h*u)/(1-h*u), with h cast to R; its denominator is positive under the hypotheses. The tree t is the actual returned construction. The statement does not assert F(t)=xs, uniqueness of ps, or any sign condition on leaf values.

targets.name: Bhola.algorithm_offset
targets.statement: For every err: N x N -> R, every k in N, and every finite real list xs, set n=length(xs) and L=length(rounds(err,k,map(leaf,xs))). Then floor((L+1)/2)=ceil(n/2^(k+1)). The left side uses natural-number integer division; the right side uses natural-number ceiling division by the positive natural number 2^(k+1). This describes the first-half length used by the next level on the tree list after k rounds. There are no nonemptiness, error-bound, or smallness hypotheses; empty xs and k=0 are included.

constructions.name: Bhola.algorithm
constructions.description: A function taking a finite list xs of reals and err: N x N -> R and returning an optional tree. Let n=length(xs) and h=clog_2(n), the natural ceiling logarithm to base 2, with clog_2(0)=0. Form map(leaf,xs), preserving the initial input order, apply rounds(err,h,that list), and return its first element as some(t), or none if the list is empty. The empty input gives none; a singleton [x] gives some(leaf(x)) with zero rounds. It constructs a tree; numerical evaluation is the separate function E. Labels are supplied by err, and the pairing rule can reorder the leaves relative to xs.

constructions.name: Bhola.rounds
constructions.description: For any err: N x N -> R, k in N, and finite tree list ts, rounds(err,0,ts)=ts and rounds(err,k+1,ts)=level(j -> err(k,j),rounds(err,k,ts)). Thus k rounds apply levels using error rows 0,1,...,k-1 in that chronological order. Each level uses the current tree list, recalculates its half-length, and starts its pairing index at zero. Empty and singleton tree lists remain unchanged by further rounds.

constructions.name: Bhola.level
constructions.description: For any e: N -> R and finite ordered tree list ts=[t_0,...,t_(n-1)], put m=floor((n+1)/2)=ceil(n/2). Output one tree for each zero-based index j with 0 <= j < m, in increasing j order: add(t_j,t_(j+m),e(j)) if j+m<n, and t_j otherwise. The output length is m. Thus it pairs entries across the two halves, at distance m, rather than adjacent entries. If n=2r+1, t_r is the unmatched tree and is placed last in the output; if n=2r every output tree is a pair. Empty input gives empty output. A paired tree has value (E(t_j)+E(t_(j+m)))*(1+e(j)) and leaf list F(t_j) concatenated with F(t_(j+m)); the unmatched tree keeps its value and leaves. For example, four initial leaves a,b,c,d produce trees with leaf lists [a,c] and [b,d]; their subsequent merge has leaf list [a,c,b,d].

assumptions: N includes zero and R is the real field. Lists are finite ordered lists and preserve multiplicities. Trees are finite objects generated by leaf: R -> Tree and add: Tree x Tree x R -> Tree. E and F denote the supplied Tree.eval and Tree.leaves definitions stated in the summary.

The supplied auxiliary function is gamma(k,u)=(k*u)/(1-k*u) for k in N and u in R, using the real cast of k. In the bounded-error target its denominator is positive. clog_2(n) denotes the natural ceiling logarithm, with value zero at n=0; all length arithmetic and round indices are natural numbers.

Only algorithm_leaf_backward_error assumes nonempty xs, real u>=0, |err(l,j)|<=u at every natural index pair (including unused pairs), and clog_2(length(xs))*u<1. The real input values otherwise have no magnitude, sign, or distinctness restriction.
algorithm_offset assumes no restrictions beyond the displayed domains. Neither target assumes floating-point arithmetic or any particular mechanism that produces err.
